channel.description: Latest articles from Nonprofit Quarterly – Bias and Credibility (nonprofitquarterly.org)

item.title: How the NAACP Is Stopping Dirty Data | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: The NAACP, alongside local communities, is gearing up to fight the long battle against AI data centers through multi-stakeholder lawsuits.

item.title: Disability Groups Are Standing United for Trans Rights. That Hasn’t Always Been the Case. | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: Disability advocates are fighting a Trump administration rule to roll back more safeguards for trans people.

item.title: Mobilizing for Haitian Immigrants in Ohio | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: Haitians in Ohio are dealing with targeted harassment, lost employment, and expired driver’s licenses as Temporary Protected Status remains vulnerable.

item.title: Of Tech Bros and Eco Collapse—Warnings from McGovern’s 99th Day | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: Gerry McGovern’s new book 99th Day: A Warning About Technology connects environmental degradation, technology, and deeply entrenched toxic masculinity.

item.title: The Ellisons’ Empire: Media Consolidation, Narrative Control, and the Threat to Democracy | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: The Ellisons’ takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery signals that narrative control can be bought. Independent newsrooms can push back.

item.title: Seat at the Table, No Vote in the Box: Finding the Governance “Sweet Spot” | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: In today’s issue of Ask a Nonprofit Expert, Cheretta Clerkley, MBA, of BoardSource, addresses a reader’s question about the appropriate levels of staff involvement on the board of directors.

item.title: As Migrant Children Remain in Federal Custody, What Can Nonprofits Do? | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: As policies shift and immigration courts face mounting backlogs, unaccompanied immigrant children are in custody far longer than the system was designed for. Jennifer Podkul of Kids in Need of Defense (KIND) weighs in on the role of nonprofits in protecting children’s rights.

item.title: Disability Inclusion Isn’t “Special Needs”—It’s Smart Philanthropy | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: The US Department of Education has gutted nearly all staff responsible for special education oversight, leaving many disability-related programs across agencies to face growing uncertainty about the future of their funding. Funders can help by leaning in on three foundational pillars for advancing disability inclusion.

item.title: What Is the SAVE America Act? | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: An explainer on the bill that would require voters to provide documents—such as US passports or birth certificates—proving their citizenship.

item.title: The Expanding Toll of the Child Detention Industry | Nonprofit Quarterly | Civic News. Empowering Nonprofits. Advancing Justice.
item.description: Since January of last year, at least 3,800 children have been detained by ICE. What’s the impact of immigration enforcement on so many children on the frontlines?
